concepts.title: Perimeter of a Shape and of a Circle
concepts.definition: Perimeter is the length of the boundary of a shape, found by adding all sides or using a formula; for a circle the perimeter is the circumference, 2 pi times the radius - the constant pi being the ratio every circle keeps between circumference and diameter.
concepts.key_idea: Walk the boundary: sides for polygons, 2 pi r for every circle.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh106.txt sections 6.1-6.2 (perimeter of a shape, perimeter of a circle)

solution_steps.explain: The circumference of a circle is 2 pi r.

concepts.title: Length of an Arc of a Circle
concepts.definition: An arc is a part of the circle's boundary, so its length is the same fraction of the circumference as its central angle is of the full turn: arc length equals angle over 360 times 2 pi r.
concepts.key_idea: Share of the turn times the whole boundary: that is the arc.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh106.txt section 6.4 (length of an arc of a circle)

solution_steps.explain: Multiply by 2 pi r for the arc length.

concepts.title: Area of Rectangle, Parallelogram and Triangle
concepts.definition: Areas stack up from the rectangle: a parallelogram straightens into a rectangle of the same base and height, and a triangle fills exactly half of its wrapping parallelogram - giving base times height for the parallelogram and half of base times height for the triangle.
concepts.key_idea: Rectangle first, parallelogram next, triangle half: one base-height story.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh106.txt sections 6.6-6.8 (areas of rectangle, parallelogram, triangle)

solution_steps.explain: This is the parallelogram area on the same base.
The triangle is half of the parallelogram.

concepts.title: Perimeter Puzzles and Paradoxes
concepts.definition: Perimeter and area tell different stories: shapes with the same perimeter can hold different areas, and shapes with the same area can need different boundaries - the relay-track and rope-shape puzzles of this chapter train the habit of separating the two measures.
concepts.key_idea: Boundary length and enclosed space are independent: one cannot decide the other.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh106.txt section 6.5 (problems, puzzles, and paradoxes on perimeter)

solution_steps.explain: Find the perimeter and the area of each shape separately.

Perimeter and area answer different questions.
